registry: Prespecified single-hypothesis tests of externally documented scout tips
why_no_fdr: The blind sweep corrects for multiplicity because it tests every cue against every contrast with no prior. These are different: each row below was written down by a professional scout before we looked at any film, naming the pitcher, the cue, the pitch contrast and the direction.
A prespecified, single-hypothesis, one-sided test of a named prediction on a named pitcher carries no multiple-comparison burden, and therefore far more power than anything in the blind sweep.
This family is kept structurally separate from the blind sweep. Results from the two must never be pooled, counted together, or presented as if they had equal prior support.
rules_fixed_in_advance: One-sided test against the direction recorded here. A result in the opposite direction is a FAILURE, not a finding with a flipped sign.
Split unchanged: disjoint on game_date, 3 most recent starts for discovery, 6 preceding for validation.
Reported per test: one-sided p, Hedges g, Youden J, likelihood ratio, precision against base rate, fire count, cell sizes.
No cue in a retracted family may be used, even if the scout named it. Retraction concerns what the instrument measures and is not overridden by documentary support.
If a direction recorded here is later found to misread the source, the correction is logged as a dated amendment, never silently edited.
